answer: Admission by lottery-drawn guarantors beats upward vouching. Each new identity gets three existing members assigned at random from the entire population, and every guarantor must post a bond that is forfeited if the newcomer defects. A cloning operation cannot pick its sponsors, so the odds that all draws land inside its own ring fall geometrically as it adds identities; it must instead recruit independent bond-posting members who genuinely risk capital. That bond is the jetty holding the flood of fakes back, not a lotus of goodwill, and any umber stain of collusion burns the whole set.
